invariants.statement: An unauthenticated request cannot observe any subject name or count.
proof: HTTP integration: both routes return the legacy 401 envelope

invariants.statement: A locked subject is invisible to ordinary users and administrators; null is_locked remains visible.
An ordinary user's identity-owned blacklist removes the same subject from names, metadata and quiz_count.
Administrators bypass user_subjects restrictions but never bypass subject locking.
Visible subjects are ordered by numeric subject ID and repeated reads preserve the same order.
proof: adapter integration with names deliberately out of lexical order

invariants.statement: Subjects with zero questions remain present with question_count 0 and do not change quiz_count.
The subject list top-level subjects and data.subjects arrays are equal by value and order.

The result count does not increase SQL statement count; the business use case uses exactly one identity-policy SELECT plus one catalog SELECT, while a normal successful HTTP request adds exactly one authentication-authority SELECT for a total of three.

GET execution performs no PostgreSQL or Redis business-state mutation and writes no application data cache. Bearer-only requests only add expiring subject-rate counters keyed by a domain-separated HMAC identity pseudonym; target Session requests may refresh Session and registry/index runtime state; first-use Flask Session exchange also creates bounded exchange/replay and target Session runtime state. No raw identity ID enters a Redis key.
proof: absence of application data cache keys

invariants.statement: Catalog never imports identity internals or queries users/user_subjects; learning-owned statistics remain outside this slice.
The 61st request in the test profile returns the observed legacy 429 envelope and required rate-limit headers; unauthenticated requests consume no identity budget.
Database and catalog failures keep route-specific empty 500 shapes while never returning exception text, credentials or internal addresses.
